findings.description: Strongest finding: the real `TAX_RESERVE_HEADER` is a 7-column kernel-exact tax-lifecycle rollup — ["Jurisdiction","Tax Year","Accrued","Moved","Paid","Outstanding","Shortfall"] — and `TAX_HEADER` is a 6-column accrual schema — ["Sale ID","Lot ID","Jurisdiction","Tax Year","Amount","Lifecycle State"]. SHEET-TAB-004 states only 'one row per accrual' / 'one row per (Jurisdiction, Tax Year)' — no column schema at all. All 3 B-outputs independently reconstructed both headers verbatim from lib.rs/tests. None of the 3 A-outputs (spec-text-only) anticipated the 5-figure lifecycle breakdown: A1 invented a single reserve_amount column, A2 a single reserved_cents column, A3 a single summed reserved column — all collapsing what the real code exposes as five distinct kernel-exact figures into one aggregate. The spec is silent on what the reserve summary even reconciles; the code pins a specific, much richer semantic.

Physical-separation mechanism and the VIEW_TABS accounting rule: the real code achieves 'physically separated' by making the reserve-summary band its own independently-named ViewTab (TAX_RESERVE_TAB = "Tax · Reserve Summary", own frozen header at row 1, own DATA_START_ROW=2 anchor) explicitly carved out as 'part of the Tax surface, not a fifth entry in VIEW_TABS' (VIEW_TABS.len() stays 4) — captured precisely by B2 ('shall not count as a fifth entry ... length stays 4') and B3 ('each its own ViewTab ... never nested'). None of this — separate-tab-object mechanics, the DATA_START_ROW anchor, or the VIEW_TABS-count exclusion — is stated by SHEET-TAB-004, which says only 'physically separated.' (Context, not counted as a finding: all 3 A-outputs unanimously invented the opposite mechanism — one shared 'Tax' sheet with a fixed blank-row gap constant, BAND_GAP_ROWS/GAP_ROWS = 1 or 2, between two stacked ranges. Per the A/B rules this unanimous A-side choice has no textual basis in the spec — an assumption artifact, not a spec-side finding, so this does not make the item BD.)

Value/formula typing: every cell in both Tax-tab bands is Cell::Value — the Tax view contains no Cell::Formula/GOOGLEFINANCE-dependent cell, unlike the Positions tab's live-price formula columns (kernel-exact, as-of-last-sync). SHEET-TAB-004 never mentions the value/formula boundary. Caught explicitly only by B3; B1/B2 don't contradict it, they simply don't surface it — a minor B-internal completeness gap, not a disagreement.

Missing-amount handling: when an accrual's applied_cents is None (not yet applied), the Amount cell renders as an empty string "" (a.applied_cents.map(fmt_cents).unwrap_or_default()) — never "0.00", and the row is never dropped. All 3 B-outputs converge on this exactly (B1 event-driven clause, B2 S3, B3 explicit). SHEET-TAB-004 says nothing about accrual-amount formatting or the not-yet-applied case.

Cell-value normalization rules pinned by code/tests but absent from SHEET-TAB-004: Jurisdiction renders as "Federal" or "State(code)" (jurisdiction_label); Lifecycle State collapses Accrued/Allocated{..}/Moved{..}/Paid{..} to the four bare labels (lifecycle_label, payload fields dropped); all monetary cells use the signed two-decimal fmt_cents format. All 3 B-outputs agree on these verbatim; none appear in the EARS text.

No-ragged-rows / no-among-data-row mechanics are asserted by the real tests with concrete literal checks (row length == header length; first cell non-empty; row's text sequence != TAX_RESERVE_HEADER; first cell != literal "RESERVE SUMMARY") in tax_accrual_band_has_no_among_data_summary_rows and publishes_four_view_tabs_one_row_per_entity. SHEET-TAB-004's prose states only the outcome ('never an among-data summary row'); all 3 B-outputs reconstruct essentially the same concrete checks — confirms these are test-pinned mechanics beyond the spec's prose.

notes: Read the real implementation (crates/sheets-view/src/lib.rs) and its test file (tests/tabs.rs) directly. Direction A produced three spec-text-only sketches that are largely self-aware inventions (each explicitly flags its assumptions) and, per the stated A/B rules, none of their invented content traces to explicit SHEET-TAB-004 text that the real code fails to honor — so Direction A surfaces no material finding on its own. A-internal agreement is only medium: A1/A2 agree the reserve-summary values arrive pre-aggregated from the kernel (sheets-view never sums), consistent with the crate's stated "owns no accounting or tax math" boundary; A3 breaks this by computing the sum itself inside build_tax_tab, actually violating that stated constraint, and also diverges on gap size (1 vs. 2) and omits a header field entirely. Direction B is highly stable: B1/B2/B3 independently reconstruct both real header arrays verbatim, the same formatting/normalization rules, and the same unwanted-behavior checks, differing only additively (e.g., B3 alone calls out the Cell::Value/Formula split). Net relationship: B surfaces substantial code-side surplus (concrete headers, the reserve band's five-figure lifecycle schema, the separate-ViewTab/VIEW_TABS-exclusion mechanism, value-only typing, empty-amount handling, label normalization) that SHEET-TAB-004 never states, while A's only disagreement with the real code (its invented same-sheet blank-row-gap layout) is an assumption artifact with no spec-text basis — hence B-ONLY-DRIFT rather than BD-DRIFT.
